To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the XRF technique is a reliable and fast screening method for waste analysis, and that the degree of heterogeneity is the main factor influencing the quality of the obtained XRF results.

(1) portable/handheld x ray fluorescence (X RF) systems are a suitable method for screening analysis of waste materials and for the determination of critical parameters; (2) the results of the screening analysis can be used to identify the material as hazardous waste; (3) the results are influenced by the homogeneity/hetero- geneity of the sample; and (4) the results are also influenced by the matrix effects and the spectral overlap of elements.
portable XRF systems are a valuable tool for the analysis of hazardous elements in waste, but the accuracy of the results is strongly dependent on the homogeneity/heterogenity of the waste material.

the development of new methods to determine the chemical composition of waste and the evaluation of the results of these methods in comparison with other methods of chemical waste analysis.
the development of a new method to determine the concentration of the heavy metals in waste materials, using a portable XRF instrument.
the development and validation of a new method for the analysis and classification of waste materials.
